steps.description:
You’ve had fun with conditional loops (repeat until/while). Now, you're going to learn another key logic element, the If control statement. In fact, many complex decisions in programming rely on a combination of these two fundamental methods!

An If block checks a condition and execute codes when it is true.


Let's practise the simple If block by creating the code below:

1. If Button D22 is pressed, a sound will be played.

2. If Button D22 is not pressed, nothing will happen.

3. The program will run forever to keep checking for button press.


Maybe you can ignore it if nothing is going to happen.

An If block checks a condition and execute codes when it is true.

Let's twist the logic a little and see if you can still get it.

1. If Button D22 is not pressed, a sound will be played.

2. If Button D22 is pressed, no sound will be played.

3. The program will run forever to keep checking for button press.


Pay attention to your condition.

An If block checks a condition and execute codes when it is true.


When multiple If blocks are stacked, the program will check through the conditions one at a time from top to bottom. Whenever it meets a true condition, the code within the block will run. In the example below, if all the conditions are true, then the codes will run one after another.
   

Practise using TWO If blocks to do the following:

1. If Button D22 is pressed, display "-_<" on the LCD for 0.5 second.

2. If Button D24 is pressed, display ">_-" on the LCD for 0.5 second.

3. The program will run forever to keep checking for button press.

Besides, pressing each button, try holding down both buttons for a long while and observe. You should the text alternating since both conditions are true.

You can also add Else to an If block.
   

This is how it works:
 

It may seems to be similar to using two If blocks, but the difference will be demonstrated more clearly in later challenges.

Mosquitoes are irritating but hitting them is hard! To practice your speed, you are going to build a speed training game call the Mozzie Zapper.
The game gives you 0.2 second to hit the button when "Mozzie" appears:
1. Display "Get ready" for 2 seconds.
2. Wait for Button D18 to be released. This is to make sure you can't cheat!
3. Display "Mozzie" for 0.2 second.
4. If Button D18 is pressed, display "hit", else display "miss".
5. The program ends.

Challenge your friend to see who can land a hit!

Create a flowchart of the previous step (load the snippet of your previous step's codes on a separate browser tab).

Refer to the notes on flowchart: https://tinyurl.com/TheLabHatFlowchart


Note: Flowcharts will be saved in snippets under "Diagrams and Flowcharts". If you want to continue editing a previously saved flowchart, load it from the snippets.
